A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PENCIL research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PENCIL benchmark results, heuristic-estimation experiments, ablations, and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on multiple labeled subgraphs, synthetic latent-space graphs, and node-labeling overhead.

M1.justification: The standard PENCIL architecture, tokenization, multiplicative residual, and BCE objective remain unchanged. Appendix C.5 adds a concrete experimental variant, PENCIL+LRP-3, using DeepSets-style pooling over three labeled subgraphs; v1 already discussed LRP theoretically but did not specify or evaluate this finite variant.

E1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds synthetic latent-space link prediction with controlled cluster separation and feature informativeness, including uninformative-feature and overlapping-cluster scenarios. Appendix C.7.3 adds a synthetic graph for extraction-cost evaluation. These expand the tested conditions beyond the retained real-world datasets and heuristic-estimation tasks.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged. New Table 14 directly compares unlabeled extraction with DRNL, RWPE, and LapPE, adding evaluated encoding-cost comparators. GCN, GAT, CN, and AA in the synthetic experiments already appeared in v1's evaluations.

E3.justification: The new latent-space experiments introduce a 90/10 positive-edge split, balanced evaluation pairs with negatives selected far apart in latent space, and two-layer neural models with hidden dimension 256. New studies also specify three-label pooling and extraction measurements across four sampling configurations. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and tabulated training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of whether multiple labeled subgraphs help, sensitivity to structural and feature signals, and the computational overhead of structural/positional encodings. These address additional design and applicability questions beyond the retained depth, multiplicative-residual, initialization, and runtime analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain five Planetoid seeds, three OGB seeds, existing uncertainty estimates, and timing averages over 50 batches. The added studies disclose no new repetition or uncertainty-estimation procedure; the LRP-3, synthetic-performance, and extraction-cost entries provide point estimates without accompanying uncertainty.

E6.justification: All original table values and plotted results are retained, but Tables 10–12 and 14 add substantial results. LRP-3 reports cora MRR 39.18 versus PENCIL's 42.23±1.98. On synthetic graphs, PENCIL scores 93.59 at (s=2, mu=1), but GCN exceeds it at (s=2, mu=0), 40.67 versus 36.01. Extraction timings are also newly reported; these are additional settings, not improvements over v1's benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix B.6 revises Proposition 4.5's proof to assign vectors explicitly to sampled tokens and changes the sufficient orthonormality condition from d≥|V| to d≥Nmax. This aligns the argument with the sampled-subgraph setting. The principal theorem statements and other proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims and introduction's principal contributions remain stable. Section 7 adds an explicit novelty claim about providing the first systematic explanation for vanilla Transformers' link-prediction capability and presents increasing sampling budgets as a route to greater practical expressivity.

C2.justification: v2 explains the computational tradeoff of averaging canonicalizations and interprets the pooling experiment as supporting single-subgraph prediction. It also interprets synthetic results through feature-dependent GAT attention versus PENCIL's structural tokenization, and discusses larger sampling budgets. Existing limitations concerning per-link costs, data requirements, and incomplete expressivity characterization remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code pointer, specifies orthogonal-initialization gain 1 and attention masking, and clarifies that the single-negative training ratio applies across datasets. It documents the synthetic generator and encoding configurations for the added experiments. Existing software, hardware, and benchmark hyperparameter disclosures are retained; the linked code's availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Hoff et al., Sarkar et al., Saxe et al., and two Zhao et al. works, supporting the synthetic model, heuristic motivation, initialization, and expressivity discussion. The conclusion modestly strengthens novelty positioning. Updated Lachi and Yehudai references represent the same works, not additional citations.

P1.justification: Localized additions clarify batching, initialization, residual propagation, heuristic estimation, and permutation invariance. The conclusion expands, acknowledgements appear, and new appendix subsections precede the relocated computational-complexity section. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displayed evidence with latent-geometry and distance-distribution figures and tables for pooling, synthetic performance, and encoding overhead. Existing figures and tables are retained and redistributed: v1 Figure 8 becomes Figure 10, and timing Table 10 becomes Table 13. The original displays themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves documentation and evidential support through the code pointer, corrected sampled-token orthogonality condition, and targeted pooling, feature-sensitivity, and encoding-cost studies. The gains are limited by missing uncertainty for the added results and deliberately well-separated synthetic negatives, which restrict broader conclusions. The core benchmark evidence and principal theoretical results remain largely unchanged.
